walkthroughs.body_html: Guru Nanak was born in 1469 in what is now Pakistan. He taught that there is one God (Waheguru), all people are equal, and we should serve others. His teachings became the basis of Sikhism.

After Guru Nanak came nine more human Gurus. The tenth, Guru Gobind Singh, declared that the holy book — the Guru Granth Sahib — would be the eternal Guru after him. So Sikhs follow ten human Gurus and one scripture Guru.

Sikh worship happens in a gurdwara. Anyone can enter — they remove their shoes and cover their head. The langar is a free meal served to anyone, of any background. It shows the Sikh belief in equality and service (seva).

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.

It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
